name: John Birch Society

summary.text: The John Birch Society was founded by retired candy manufacturer Robert Welch in Indianapolis on December 9, 1958, after a two-day meeting with eleven business and professional men, most of whom became founding members; Brown University's library, which holds the society's records, lists Fred Koch of Koch Industries and Robert Waring Stoddard of Wyman-Gordon among the original twelve founding members. The society describes itself as chartered under Massachusetts law as a not-for-profit educational organization.

sources.title: John Birch Society records at the John Hay Library

facts.claim: The society's own timeline says Robert Welch founded it on December 9, 1958 in Indianapolis, Indiana; a JBS booklet says Welch met with eleven business and professional men, most of whom became founding members.
facts.quote: Robert Welch founded The John Birch Society on December 9, 1958 in Indianapolis, Indiana

facts.claim: Brown University's John Hay Library, holder of the society's records, lists the original twelve founding members including Fred Koch, founder of Koch Industries, and Robert Waring Stoddard, president of Wyman-Gordon.

sources.title: John Birch Society records at the John Hay Library

facts.claim: The society says it is chartered under Massachusetts general law as a not-for-profit educational organization; Welch led it until 1983, when Congressman Larry McDonald became chairman.
facts.quote: chartered under Massachusetts general law as a not-for-profit educational organization
